value: Oland, C.B. (2004). Guide to Combined Heat and Power Systems for Boiler Owners and Operators. ORNL/TM-2004/144, July 30, 2004. Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Oak Ridge, Tennessee.

Targeted extraction. Loaded (main): Table 3.1 prime mover characteristics for six CHP prime movers (steam turbine, gas turbine, microturbine, compression- and spark-ignition reciprocating engines, phosphoric acid fuel cell): capacity range (MW, electric), heat-to-power ratio (derived as the inverse of the printed power-to-heat ratio), installed cost $/kW, maintenance cost $/kWh, total CHP efficiency and electrical efficiency (both HHV, as printed), availability and service life. Table 3.1 cites Refs. 2 and 4-8 of Chapter 3: the Energy Nexus Group Technology Characterizations prepared for US EPA in 2002 (steam turbines, gas turbines, microturbines, reciprocating engines, fuel cells) and DOE (2000) Combined Heat and Power: A Federal Manager's Resource Guide. None of these originals is held in the repo (checked source-details_sources.csv), so the values go in the main file with "reprinted from" notes. No price year is printed: 2004 publication year used (the 2002 originals likely use 2000-2002 dollars). Other-values: rejected-heat temperatures (degF) and overhaul periods from Table 3.1; Table 7.1 typical CHP system performance (reprinted from OTA 1983, too old for the main file). Not loaded: regulatory chapters, codes and standards tables, emission control technique tables, payback tables 8.2-8.4 (illustrative calculations at assumed $500 and $2,000/kW). Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 24). Traps: steam-turbine installed cost likely excludes the boiler; steam-turbine electrical efficiency 20-40% HHV is on boiler fuel and covers condensing/extraction designs, high for a pure back-pressure turbine; maintenance figures are "up to" for steam turbine and microturbine (max only); fuel-cell maintenance excludes stack replacement; table basis is systems operating at least 8,000 h/yr.
